statement: A vocabulary built to credit a repository is not safe to reuse for accusing one. 2026-11-19: #741's B3 reader named workflows in which 'a failing test command is ignored'. It decided a line ran tests by matching CI_TEST_COMMAND_PATTERN anywhere on the line. That pattern credits CI test commands, so a loose match there only over-credits. Reused to assert a defect, it named `pip install pytest pytest-cov || true`, `mkdir -p jest-results || true` and `rm -f jest.config.js || true` as ignored test runs, and it ignored later lines that fail the step on the result (`! grep -q FAILED out.log`). Both CI and the PR's 396-pair comparison were green: every fixture had been built to match. Fix: a reader that asserts a defect anchors on the command word, abstains on anything it cannot place (heredocs, folded blocks, keys not the step's own, job-level semantics it has not verified), and gets negative fixtures written by someone other than its author.
